packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 07 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification or reading of this item reached me before or during the work. My context held only the task brief and PROMPT.md. This is a blind reading.
- Every image (image-001 to image-026) loaded. I viewed each one.
- Visible on the leaves and photographed with them: modern pencil shelfmark notes. Face 1 has one at bottom right, reading "Stams, StA, Frag. 48r(?)". Face 2 has "Stams, StA, Frag. 48v". The paper sheet photographed above face 2 carries "Stams, StA, Adl. 1v zu Frag. 48v". These are archive labels in the images, not identifications of the text.
- One step went beyond the rules: on face 2 the text is upside down in the supplied images. To read it I made rotated (180 degrees) copies of image-014 to image-026 in my own scratch directory, plus some enlarged (2x) crops of those copies. Nothing outside the packet images was opened. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.
- LINE NUMBERING: for face 2, line numbers count from the TOP OF THE ROTATED (upright-text) view, so from the BOTTOM of the image as supplied. Lines are approximate counts of the visible written lines within each tile.

=====================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
=====================================================================
FACE 1 (overview image-001; tiles image-002 to image-013)
- A parchment fragment re-used as a binding wrapper or cover. It has fold lines along all four sides, chamfered (cut-off) corners, and a long rectangular slot cut out of the centre. The slot is repaired with clear tape at both ends. Worm or insect holes run through it.
- No main text visible. This is the blank, outer side of the wrapper. Some faint grey offset or show-through appears in places (e.g. image-009 centre), but I could read no letters.
- At left, a paper strip/label is attached. It has modern pencil notes, written vertically:
  image-002: "Cod(?) 1966" or "Reg(?) 1966" (rotated pencil, partly masked)
  image-010: "(53) / 1 3. Januar" and "...[ver?]pfl(?)ichtun(?)" or "Vorpfluten(?)" (pencil, uncertain); below, "6 x 7(?)"
  These are modern archival/cataloguing notes. A grey mask covers most of the label.
- image-012/013 bottom right: pencil "Stams, StA, Frag. 48r(?)" (last letter uncertain).

FACE 2 (overview image-014; tiles image-015 to image-026)
- The written side. In the supplied orientation it is UPSIDE DOWN (180 degrees). Rotating it gives normal script orientation: ascenders up, line-initial capitals at the left.
- Script: German cursive documentary hand (Kurrent-type), apparently one hand in brown ink. Language: German. Long-line text, ONE column. The lines once ran across the full width of the sheet. The central cut-out slot now interrupts every line in the middle, so each line has a left part (left of the slot) and a right part.
- In the rotated view, the left edge has several lines beginning with enlarged, flourished capitals hanging into the margin: a "U/V"-shaped "Und" repeated 3 times, then "Also" (image-022 rotated). These look like paragraph or clause openings.
- Top left (image-026 rotated): an enlarged decorated initial built from strapwork/loops in the margin. It may be "H" or "B" and spans about 4 lines. Beside it is a hatched lattice ornament.
- Right side (image-015 rotated): a flourished mark that might be a signature or notarial-type paraph ("...ff..." with loops) at the end of the text block. Uncertain.
- No rubrics or interlinear glosses seen. Interpretation (tentative): a vernacular legal/administrative document, such as a sale, conveyance or agreement. This rests on words like "Kauff", "verkaufft", "bezalt" and "gelegen" below. I have not inferred the work, date or provenance.
- Condition: strong staining and abrasion. The central third (image-020/021 area) is badly rubbed and almost unreadable. Fold lines run across the text near top and bottom. Wormholes.

=====================================================================
AREAS SELECTED AND READ
=====================================================================
Rotated view, with the supplied filenames:
 A. Upper-left block with decorated initial (image-026)
 B. Upper block just left of the slot (image-025)
 C. Left margin "Und / Und / Und / Also" clause openings (image-022)
 D. Upper-right block, right of the slot (image-023)
 E. Middle-right block (image-019)
 F. Lower-left block (image-018 / image-017), partly
Left largely unread: the central rubbed zone (image-020, image-021), most of image-024, the lower right (image-016, image-015) beyond a few words, and the lines under the tape repairs.

Conventions: (?) = uncertain reading. [illegible] = could not read. Expansions in parentheses. I have not normalised spelling.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

=====================================================================
LIMITATIONS
=====================================================================
- The central slot removes the middle of every line on face 2. Left and right halves cannot be joined as continuous text from these images except by assumption, and I have not made that assumption.
- Most proposed words carry (?). The hand is a rapid cursive with heavy abrasion, and many readings are letter-shape guesses, not secure word readings.
- Line numbers apply to the rotated view (counted from the bottom edge of the supplied images). The adjacent tiles overlap, and I have flagged repeated lines as overlaps.
- Face 1 has no readable main text. Only modern pencil labels are there, partly masked.
- Would help: a raking-light or UV image of the central abraded zone (image-020/021) and of the taped areas; a higher-magnification crop of the decorated initial and the first two lines (image-026 top / image-025 top); and the right-hand flourish (image-015) to check whether it is a signature or notarial mark.
